meta.title: Windows event IDs: 4624, 4625, 4740 (cheatsheet)
meta.description: Cheatsheet of Windows events useful for security and troubleshooting: 4624, 4625, 4740, 4672, 7045, 1102, with log, meaning and PowerShell query.
meta.intro: The events to know to audit sign-ins, accounts, services and unexpected shutdowns, with the log concerned and the Get-WinEvent query to find them.
meta.card: 4624, 4625, 4740, 4672, 7045, 1102, 41 and more: log, meaning, PowerShell query.
meta.notice: The Security log needs an elevated prompt, and event auditing must be enabled by policy (Advanced Audit Policy Configuration).

entries.name: 4624: successful sign-in
entries.desc: An account signed in. The type tells how: 2 interactive, 3 network, 4 batch, 5 service, 7 unlock, 10 remote desktop (RDP), 11 cached credentials.
entries.pitfall: Very voluminous (machine accounts, services). Filter on type 10 for RDP, or type 3 for network access.

entries.name: 4625: failed sign-in
entries.desc: A sign-in attempt failed. The sub status gives the cause: 0xC000006A wrong password, 0xC0000064 account does not exist, 0xC0000234 account locked, 0xC0000072 account disabled, 0xC000006F outside allowed hours.
entries.pitfall: Many failures from the same IP address on 3389 or 445 point to a brute-force attack.

entries.name: 4634 / 4647: sign-out
entries.desc: End of a session. Match the session ID (Logon ID) with the one from 4624 to compute the duration.
entries.pitfall: A 4634 without a 4647 matches an automatic logoff (timeout or shutdown).

entries.name: 4648: sign-in with explicit credentials
entries.desc: A session used credentials other than the user's own (runas, scheduled task, drive mapping).
entries.pitfall: Useful to detect lateral movement, but also very frequent in normal use.

entries.name: 4768 / 4769 / 4771: Kerberos
entries.desc: Kerberos events on domain controllers. 4771 with code 0x18 signals a wrong password.
entries.pitfall: A surge of 4769 with RC4 encryption (0x17) can reveal Kerberoasting.

entries.name: 4776: NTLM validation
entries.desc: The domain controller validated credentials through NTLM. Error code 0xC000006A means wrong password.
entries.pitfall: Many 4776 events point to applications still using NTLM instead of Kerberos.

entries.name: 4740: account lockout
entries.desc: An account was locked out. The 'Caller Computer Name' field names the machine that caused the wrong passwords.
entries.pitfall: Query the controller that holds the PDC role. The source machine often keeps an old password (session, mapped drive, mobile).

entries.name: 4720 / 4722 / 4725 / 4726: account lifecycle
entries.desc: Creation, enabling, disabling and deletion of a user account.
entries.pitfall: Check who acted (the 'Subject' field) and compare with the official creation or leaver requests.

entries.name: 4723 / 4724: password change or reset
entries.syn: 4723 (changed by the user) · 4724 (reset by an administrator)
entries.desc: A password was changed or reset.
entries.pitfall: A reset (4724) outside working hours or by an unusual account deserves a check.

entries.name: 4728 / 4732 / 4756: added to a group
entries.desc: A member was added to a security group. Watch above all Administrators, Domain Admins and Enterprise Admins.
entries.pitfall: Removals match events 4729, 4733 and 4757.

entries.name: 4672: special privileges assigned
entries.desc: A session received sensitive privileges (for example SeDebugPrivilege). Normal for administrator accounts and SYSTEM.
entries.pitfall: A non-administrator account in this log is an alert to investigate.

entries.name: 4688: process creation
entries.desc: A process started. With the 'Include command line' option, the event contains the arguments.
entries.pitfall: The command line must be enabled by GPO (Audit Process Creation + Include command line).

entries.name: 1102: audit log cleared
entries.desc: The security log was cleared. This event is always recorded, even if auditing is off.
entries.pitfall: Clearing logs is a classic technique to hide an intrusion: forward logs to a central collector.

entries.name: 4719: audit policy changed
entries.desc: The system audit policy changed.

entries.name: 4697 / 7045: service installed
entries.desc: A new service was installed. Malware and remote execution tools (PsExec) create them.
entries.pitfall: Examine the executable's path: a service in a temporary folder or user profile is suspicious.

entries.name: 7034 / 7036 / 7031: service state
entries.desc: Service state changes and crashes.
entries.pitfall: A repeated 7034 means a service crashing in a loop: also check the Application log (1000, application error).

entries.name: 4698 / 4702: scheduled task created or changed
entries.desc: Creation and modification of scheduled tasks, a common persistence technique.
entries.pitfall: Requires the 'Other Object Access Events' audit.

entries.name: 41 (Kernel-Power): restart without a clean shutdown
entries.desc: The system restarted without shutting down cleanly (power loss, crash, freeze).
entries.pitfall: If BugcheckCode is 0, the cause is a power cut or a freeze: look at the hardware. A non-zero code matches a blue screen.

entries.name: 6005 / 6006 / 6008: log start and stop
entries.desc: Start and stop markers of the Event Log service, useful to reconstruct availability.

entries.name: 1074: shutdown or restart initiated
entries.desc: Shows which process or user requested the shutdown or restart, and the reason.
entries.pitfall: Answers 'who restarted the server?': the message contains the account and the reason.

entries.name: 1000 / 1001: application crash
entries.desc: An application stopped abruptly; the faulting module is shown in the message.
entries.pitfall: Note the 'Faulting module name': if it is always the same, update or reinstall that component.

entries.name: 55 / 98 (Ntfs) · 7 (disk): disk errors
entries.syn: 55 (Ntfs: corrupt structure) · 7 and 11 (disk: bad block, controller error)
entries.desc: File system or disk errors. Disk events 7, 11 or 51 often announce a disk at end of life.
entries.pitfall: Back up before running chkdsk /r on a disk showing these errors.

entries.name: 0xC000006D · 0xC000006A · 0xC0000064: sign-in status codes
entries.desc: Status and sub status codes of a 4625 event. 0xC000006D gives the status; the sub status gives the reason.
entries.pitfall: The sub status is more precise than the status: read it first.

entries.name: 0xC0000234 · 0xC0000072 · 0xC0000193: account locked, disabled, expired
entries.desc: Common sub statuses of a failed sign-in that explain why a user cannot get in.
entries.pitfall: For a locked account, then look for event 4740 on the PDC.

entries.name: Blue screen codes: 0x0000007E · 0x00000050 · 0x0000009F
entries.desc: Frequent stops: 0x7E often points to a driver, 0x50 to memory or a driver, 0x9F to a driver's power management.
entries.pitfall: Minidump files can be read with WinDbg or BlueScreenView; start by updating recent drivers.
